apps.description: A native terminal for Ainkrad — command blocks, theme-matched colors, SwiftTerm-backed.
apps.author: Ahmed M. Elhalaby
apps.longDescription:
Rune brings a full, native command line into your Ainkrad workspace — built on a SwiftTerm-backed emulator, not a web view.

• Command blocks — each command and its output is a distinct, scrollable block you can navigate, re-run, and reason about, instead of one endless stream.
• Theme-matched — colors are driven by the host's DesignTokens, so the terminal always matches your active Ainkrad theme; switch themes and it restyles instantly without losing scrollback.
• Real emulation — a proper PTY underneath: interactive programs, colors, resizing, and control sequences all work as expected.
• Fits the workspace — open it as a floating island, resize freely, and run several alongside your other apps.

Designed to feel like part of the OS surface — seamless chrome, no separator lines, traffic-lights inside the window.

apps.description: A full HUD Git IDE for Ainkrad — changes, history, branches, PRs, issues, worktrees, and an interactive commit graph.
apps.author: Ahmed M. Elhalaby
apps.longDescription:
Git Mage is a complete Git workspace for Ainkrad, wrapped in a gaming-HUD interface that feels like part of the OS.

Workspace
• Multi-repo library — add as many repositories as you like and switch between them (GitHub-Desktop style), each remembering its own state.
• Three-pane shell — a nav rail into Changes, History, Stashes, Pull Requests, Issues, Worktrees and Advanced, with full-surface repo and branch management overlays.

Everyday Git
• Changes — stage/unstage/discard by file or all at once, with a live commit box.
• History — paginated commit log that loads as you scroll, with a git-graph rail.
• Branches & Stashes — create, checkout, delete; stash push/pop/apply/drop with per-stash diffs.

Review
• GitHub-style diff viewer — syntax highlighting, line-number gutter, background-only add/remove tints, and collapsible per-file diffs shared across Changes, History, Stashes and PRs.
• Interactive worktree commit graph — a real multi-lane branch/merge graph; click any commit to inspect its diff.

GitHub
• Pull Requests & Issues — search, label filters and pagination via the GitHub API; Conversation / Commits / Files tabs; markdown descriptions and comments; review, merge, comment, close/reopen, labels and assignees.

Advanced
• Cherry-pick, revert, reset, rebase and tag management — contextual to the commit you select, with confirm-gated destructive ops.

Made yours
• Configurable keyboard shortcuts for every action and area, and a configurable typography theme (font family + size) applied live across the whole app.

apps.description: Save SSH connections and keys, open a session in one click, and summon it as an overlay — a Termius-style hub for Ainkrad.
apps.author: Ahmed M. Elhalaby
apps.longDescription:
Leyline is a home for your SSH connections and keys inside Ainkrad, summoned as a floating HUD overlay.

• Connections — save your hosts (label, host, port, username) in a flat, type-to-filter list, with password or key authentication.
• Key vault — import SSH private keys by file or paste, with an optional passphrase; keys are stored in the macOS Keychain and reused across connections.
• One-click connect — pick a connection and it opens a live session in the Ainkrad Rune over ssh; copy the ssh command any time.
• Overlay — summon Leyline as a floating HUD over your workspace, styled to match your active theme.

Your secrets stay safe: passwords, private-key material and passphrases live only in the macOS Keychain, never in the saved connection metadata.

apps.description: Markdown-native notes for Ainkrad — linked notes, backlinks, full-text search, and import from Apple Notes and Obsidian.
apps.author: Ahmed M. Elhalaby
apps.longDescription:
Lore is a markdown-native notes workspace for Ainkrad. Your notes are plain .md files in a folder you choose — nothing is locked in a database, and the files stay yours.

• Files are the source of truth — every note is a .md file with YAML frontmatter (id, title, tags, dates); edit them here or in any other editor and Lore reconciles.
• Linked notes — [[wikilinks]] with completion as you type, a backlinks panel on every note, and links that follow a file when it is renamed.
• Import what you already have — bring in an Obsidian vault or your Apple Notes library. Lore shows you every file it would write before it writes anything, flags what a conversion cannot carry over, and skips whatever you have already imported, so running it twice never duplicates your notes.
• Instant search — a local SQLite/FTS5 index mirrors your folder for fast full-text search across titles and bodies, rebuildable at any time.
• Quick capture — press ⌘N to open a fresh note focused for typing, saved to disk immediately; the fast path for fleeting thoughts.
• Live-preview editor — a native TextKit 2 editor styles markdown in place as you type: headings, bold/italic, inline code, links, checkboxes and embedded images.
• Stays in sync — an external change to an open note surfaces a non-destructive reload prompt, so edits from other tools never clobber your work.
• Theme-matched — colors come from the host's design tokens, so Lore restyles instantly with your active Ainkrad theme; seamless chrome, no separator lines.

Apple Notes import asks Notes.app directly and needs your permission under Privacy & Security → Automation. Encrypted (locked) notes are not imported.

apps.description: A native mail client for Ainkrad — IMAP/SMTP and Gmail, with a real offline outbox.
apps.author: Ahmed M. Elhalaby
apps.longDescription:
Raven brings mail into the Ainkrad workspace as a first-class surface, not a browser tab.

Accounts
• Connect Gmail with one click — OAuth credentials ship with the build, so there is nothing to paste.
• Any IMAP/SMTP host by hand, with STARTTLS on a real socket.

Sending that survives reality
• A durable outbox — compose and send with no connection, and the queue drains when you are back.
• Per-entry delivery: one message failing does not block or duplicate the rest, and mutations survive a relaunch rather than silently reverting.

Reading
• Proper conversation threading, with search across threads.
• Delta sync and backfill, so a large mailbox fills in without blocking the first read.

Fits the workspace
• Themed by the host's DesignTokens, and sits alongside your other apps rather than taking over the screen.

apps.description: Projects, epics, work items and subtasks for Ainkrad — five surfaces, and an MCP surface the assistant can actually drive.
apps.author: Ahmed M. Elhalaby
apps.longDescription:
Quest is a work tracker built into Ainkrad — projects, epics, items and subtasks, with five ways to look at them.

Five surfaces
• Today — a cross-project inbox of what is due or overdue, plus quick capture.
• Overview, List, Board and Timeline — the same work, seen the way the moment needs.

A model that holds its shape
• Three levels, capped: a project holds epics, an epic holds items (task, bug, story, chore, spike), an item holds subtasks. A move that would exceed three levels, or file something under its own descendant, is refused rather than silently accepted.
• Per-project status schemes — board columns belong to the project, not to the app. Software projects get Backlog/Todo/In Progress/In Review/Done; general projects drop In Review. Renaming a status keeps its identity, and removing one that still holds work requires saying where that work goes.
• Typed links — file, folder, url, repo, branch, PR and commit. Repo-scoped links always carry which repo they belong to, because multi-repo projects are the normal case.

Nothing disappears
• Soft delete throughout: trashing a project or item hides it everywhere but keeps it restorable from the Trash surface.

For the assistant
• A full-control MCP surface, so Ainkrad can file, move and close real work instead of writing markdown about it.
